conditions.overall: Small headwater streams in WNC are fishing best as valley rivers run low, clear, and warm. The Watauga has returned to normal summer flows after 3 weeks of high water, and the South Holston has been running low with 3 short daily pulses.

tactics: Fish small headwater streams during summer — they stay cooler, have more elevation change, and keep water well oxygenated.
Use a dry dropper setup on wild streams and keep the flies small and light. Throwing a huge dry fly will spook fish just like throwing an indicator would.
After rain events, target dingy, slightly elevated water on wild streams with small Pat's Rubber Legs (#12-14) and squirmy worms; size up to a #12 Chernobyl to float the heavier flies.
Use the North Carolina Interactive Trout Map to find new wild trout streams in the area.

On the Watauga, fish light dry dropper setups. The cold morning pulse (typically 6–7 AM) makes fish very happy and eager to feed. Generation starts at 1 PM Monday–Friday and noon on Saturday; no generation on Sunday except the morning pulse.
On the South Holston, fish light dry dropper setups during low water and don't be afraid to lengthen your leader and use light tippet (6x–6.5x) — fish can be spooky under low water conditions.
Always check current dam release schedules from TVA before heading out — flows can change without notice.

waters.name: WNC Small Headwater Streams (Wild Water)
waters.note: It's small stream season — headwater streams are producing the best results, staying cooler and well oxygenated. Use a dry dropper setup with small, light flies and a stealthy approach.

waters.name: Watauga River (East Tennessee)
waters.note: After 3 straight weeks of high water, the Watauga has returned to normal summer flows — low water in the morning with an hour-long pulse from 6–7 AM and high water in the afternoon. Fishing has been excellent; fish light dry dropper setups. Sporadic sulphur hatches still occurring in the morning.

waters.name: South Holston River (East Tennessee)
waters.note: Flows have been low for the last few weeks with 3 pulses each day, typically an hour at a time — great for wade fishing. Fish a light dry dropper and use long leaders with light tippet (6x–6.5x) as fish can be spooky in low water.

elevation_note: High Country streams (Boone, 3300-4000ft) run 1-2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC
